mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day SPX returns are positive in >50% of cases when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative economic growth and S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive in >40% of cases with these labor conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) in a late-cycle expansion signals reduced consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but SPX returns are positive, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises but SPX returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 210 indicates high inflation, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 210 but SPX returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies rise but SPX returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates during a tightening cycle increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rise but SPX returns are positive, the hypothesis is invalid.
